TypeSafe gives you $5 of API credit when you sign up

At Jev's pricing, that is basically never ending…



Why? Because Jev is priced at $0.042 per million input tokens

And output is free



So that $5 credit gives you roughly 119 million input tokens. That is why people are joking that they will pass their Jev credits down to their children, haha.



What makes it interesting is that Jev just makes decisions. You give it context, plus a fixed set of options, and it tells you what to do next



That is exactly why it is so useful.



Instead of paying a big model to generate a wall of text you will barely use, Jev can do the small, high-volume decisions inside the workflow, for example:



→ which support team gets this ticket

→ which model should handle this prompt

→ is this output safe or risky

→ should the agent call this tool or not

→ which ad fits this category

→ which alert is real and which one is noise

→ which rows should I keep, rank, or drop



People are already using it for browser agents, model routing, Postgres filtering, security workflows, and 10s of other use cases.



And the economics are what driving all the hype behind Jev. Of course, the market will test the speed and cost claims harder over time



But even right now, the direction is obvious



If GPT and Claude are the brains writing the options, Jev can be the tiny decision layer choosing the next move



And honestly, that may end up being one of the most useful pieces of the stack.
